papers.title: Aspect‐Ratio Preserving Target‐Matrix Optimization With Linesweep Smoothing for Arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian Meshes With Adaptive Refinement
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT We present a rezoning method for three‐dimensional arbitrary Lagrangian–Eulerian (ALE) and ALE with adaptive mesh refinement (ALE‐AMR) simulations. The method combines linesweep smoothing with an aspect‐ratio‐preserving target‐matrix optimization paradigm (TMOP) formulation. It is designed to preserve anisotropic mesh structures produced by the Lagrangian phase while maintaining mesh validity and reducing shear, sliver formation, and cell bunching in block‐structured, optionally nonconformal meshes. The approach combines a patch‐local TMOP objective and a convexity‐based disentanglement metric within an existing linesweep framework. The TMOP target matrix is built from local edge geometry and includes a prescribed aspect‐ratio cap, which provides an explicit control parameter for mesh relaxation. The metric is evaluated on an extended nodal patch, so that the objective couples the motion of a node to the quality of neighboring elements affected by that motion. Combined with sequential updates, this ensures that accepted steps are tested against the updated quality of the local coupled patch, rather than only against the elements directly incident on the node. When invalid configurations are detected, the TMOP objective is replaced by a convexity objective that drives signed volumes back to positive values. Parallelism is recovered through a distance‐1 coloring of the nodal graph, allowing independent node updates to be performed concurrently. Mesh‐only and hydrodynamic tests assess shear reduction, aspect‐ratio control, and mesh validity. Among the configurations examined, only the TMOP combined method consistently satisfies these requirements together while retaining anisotropic mesh structures, with no observed invalid post‐rezoning states. The prescribed target cap provides explicit control over excessive elongation without imposing an isotropic target. Strong and weak scaling measurements quantify the cost of the parallel optimization.

papers.title: Mechanisms of Geo‐Stress and Gas Pressure in Coal and Gas Outburst: Insights From Particle‐Fluid Coupled Numerical Simulation
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT With increasing mining depths, elevated geo‐stress and gas pressure substantially raise the risk of coal and gas outbursts (CGO), posing serious threats to mining safety. Conventional approaches including triaxial mechanical experiments, large‐scale physical simulations, and existing numerical models have been limited in delineating the distinct roles of geo‐stress and gas pressure during the CGO process. In this study, we developed a novel method coupling particle flow with computational fluid dynamics to unravel the underlying CGO mechanisms. Our simulations reveal that geo‐stress predominately accelerates damage via tensile and shear cracking, whereas gas pressure exerts a comparatively modest effect on crack propagation. Under coupled geo‐stress and gas pressure, the CGO failure zone evolves from a spindle‐like to a quarter‐ellipsoidal morphology. The internal stress of coal body change appears in four forms: continuous decrease, increase‐then‐decrease, continuous increase, and periodic decrease–increase. Furthermore, the increase in gas pressure and geo‐stress not only leads to higher velocity and greater quantity of outburst coal particles but also accelerates the formation of cracks, promotes earlier coal damage, and premature stress release. These findings provide mechanistic insights into the initiation and evolution of CGO, offering a quantitative basis for the design of targeted prevention strategies in deep mining.

papers.title: Targeted Therapeutic Efficacy of Three-Layer Core–Shell VPPS Composite Nanogel Against Proliferative Enteropathy Induced by Lawsonia intracellularis
papers.abstract: The obligate intracellular parasitic nature of Lawsonia intracellularis (L. intracellularis) enables it to evade host immune clearance and conventional antimicrobial action, leading to considerable therapeutic challenges and high recurrence rates. Current strategies, including vaccination and conventional antibiotic therapy, remain constrained by incomplete protection and insufficient intracellular drug delivery, underscoring the urgent need for novel oral targeted delivery strategies. Thus, the valnemulin-derived carbon dots were prepared via a hydrothermal method and sequentially encapsulated with poloxamer, high-methoxyl pectin, and sucrose to assemble a three-layer core–shell VPP NPs to address these limitations. The VPPS NPs was optimized using response surface methodology and systematically evaluated the resulting system for physicochemical properties, pH and pectinase dual-responsive release behavior, targeted antibacterial efficacy, and in vivo therapeutic performance and biosafety. Physicochemical characterization showed that VPPS NPs had a typical core–shell structure and a three-dimensional porous network with a final particle size of 122.9 ± 8.7 nm, and Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy and X-ray diffraction confirmed successful assembly and intermolecular interactions among the components. In vitro release studies revealed pH/pectinase dual-responsive release behavior, characterized by partial acid resistance in simulated gastric fluid (11.4 ± 1.6% cumulative release at 2 h) and rapid release in the neutral intestinal environment (97.8 ± 2.0% at pH 7.4), with release significantly accelerated in the presence of pectinase (72.4 ± 1.7% vs. 32.8 ± 2.8% without pectinase). VPPS NPs were efficiently internalized by intestinal epithelial cells, resulting in substantially higher intracellular drug accumulation than free drug (25.2 ± 2.9 μg/mg protein vs. 0.03 ± 0.003 μg/mg protein), and could directly disrupt the cell wall and membrane structures of intracellular L. intracellularis. Furthermore, VPPS NPs achieved 100% survival and cure rates in infected mice, which are significantly higher than those of the commercial VH solution (70% and 50%, respectively), while restoring intestinal barrier function, alleviating oxidative stress, and modulating inflammatory responses. Biosafety evaluation confirmed the favorable biosafety profile of VPPS NPs. Collectively, VPPS NPs accomplished efficient targeted therapy against L. intracellularis infection through multi-level synergistic actions, offering an innovative strategy and technological platform for the oral treatment of proliferative enteropathy.

papers.title: Low-Temperature-Conditioned Biogenic Calcite from Waste Eggshells in Metakaolin Geopolymer Gels: Structural, Textural and Functional Properties
papers.abstract: Hen eggshell is an abundant, calcite-rich food waste that is usually valorised by calcination at 800–1000 °C, an energy-intensive step that releases its carbonate CO2 and destroys its biogenic microstructure. Low-temperature routes that keep the calcite intact have received little attention, and their effect on the structure and functions of geopolymer gels is unknown. This work examined whether eggshell conditioned at only 250 °C (ES-250) can replace 10 wt% of the metakaolin in a geopolymer gel, and what it changes. ES-250 remained pure biogenic calcite, with intracrystalline vesicles and residual organic matter, and the route needs ≈3–6 times less heat than calcination, including drying. In the hardened binder, ES-250 persisted as discrete 2–5 µm calcite particles without detectable Ca diffusion into the aluminosilicate gel. The Si–O–T bonding, the total pore volume and the N2-accessible porosity (≈41%) were preserved, and only the BET surface area decreased (36.2 → 31.6 m2 g−1). Dye uptake in the dark was maintained, but the strong antibacterial effect of the plain geopolymer, which left no culturable Escherichia coli after 4 h, was largely lost (22–34% reduction). Low-temperature-conditioned eggshell is therefore a decarbonation-free, structurally inert filler for geopolymer gels, but not a functional additive.

papers.title: Plant-Derived Bioactive Hydrogels for Cutaneous Applications: Extract Standardization, Formulation Design, and Biological Evidence
papers.abstract: Plant-derived hydrogels are promising topical delivery systems and wound dressings, but their performance depends on both the botanical preparation and the polymer matrix. This narrative review examines cutaneous formulations containing Aloe vera, Matricaria chamomilla, Centella asiatica, Vitis vinifera skin extracts, and curcumin associated with Curcuma longa, focusing on ingredient characterization, formulation design, release, and biological evidence. The reviewed studies show that hydrogel composition influences swelling, mechanical properties, and bioactive release. Biological findings include antioxidant and antimicrobial activity, cellular responses, and wound-healing-related outcomes in animal models. However, comparisons are limited by inconsistent extract characterization, incomplete dose reporting, heterogeneous biological models, and variable controls. Asiaticoside release does not represent the behavior of the entire Centella extract, while the contribution of chamomile cannot be isolated in formulations containing silver sulfadiazine. Similarly, the benefits of hydrogel incorporation over simpler formulations remain insufficiently established, and human evidence for the specific systems is limited. Future studies should prioritize reproducible extract characterization, accurate measurement of active content, appropriate component controls, and dose-matched comparisons linking release to biological outcomes. These steps are essential to determine the added value of hydrogel delivery and support clinical evaluation.

papers.title: Hybrid Chitosan/PVA Hydrogels Incorporating Silver Nanoparticles as Antibacterial Polymeric Dressings
papers.abstract: Silver nanoparticles are widely incorporated into polymer dressings, but the effect of the nanoparticle synthesis conditions on the final material is rarely compared within one polymer matrix. Here, citrate-stabilized Ag NPs were prepared by NaBH4 reduction using two reductant volumes (400 and 1000 µL) and incorporated into the same chitosan (CH)/poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) matrix cast with citric acid. UV-Vis, DLS, STEM, AFM and XRD showed face-centered cubic Ag NPs with mean diameters of 27 ± 5 nm (1000 µL) and 38 ± 6 nm (400 µL) by STEM, with the same trend by DLS and AFM. Their antibacterial effect was assessed using agar diffusion tests. In agar diffusion tests, the smaller Ag NPs gave larger inhibition zones against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus The corresponding hydrogel with smaller Ag NPs confirmed the antibacterial tests performed on nanoparticles and gave larger inhibition zones for both bacterial strains. The integration of Ag NPs in hydrogels was confirmed by SEM-EDX mapping, while their integrity was assessed using swelling tests and Ag NPs release tests. In PBS, all films, including the Ag-free control, remained intact for 48 h, with the highest swelling ratio for CH/PVA/Ag-NaBH4 1000.After 24 h in PBS at 37 °C, about 75% (CH/PVA/Ag-NaBH4 1000) and 53% (CH/PVA/Ag-NaBH4 400) of the incorporated Ag NPs were released. The CH/PVA/Ag-NaBH4 1000 formulation is therefore the more promising candidate to be considered a favorable antibacterial polymeric dressing.

papers.title: Utilization of Rice Straw Pulp as a Reinforcing Filler in Hydroxyethyl Cellulose/Gellan Gum/Alginate Bio-Composite Gel Foams
papers.abstract: To address the environmental impact of synthetic foams, this study developed sustainable composite gel foams (CGF) based on hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC), gellan gum (GG), and sodium alginate (Al) reinforced with rice straw (RS) pulp. The CGFs were fabricated using solution casting followed by freeze-drying, with RS pulp content varied from 0% to 4% (w/v). SEM analysis revealed that RS pulps acted as physical fiber reinforcement, promoting a more interconnected and robust porous network. FTIR spectra confirmed the successful integration of RS pulp through characteristic lignin peaks at 1540 cm−1. Adding RS pulp clearly improves the foam’s mechanical strength, notably its compressive strength and Young’s modulus, over the control sample. All of these best mechanical, water retention, and structural stability properties resulted from the 2% (w/v) RS pulp addition, which was attributed to the formation of a dense, interconnected fiber-reinforcing network and tortuous microporous channels that provided high capillary resistance and physical constraints against structural deformation. Especially, the CGF exhibited exceptional water absorption capabilities, exceeding 1900% in the initial stages. The thermal stability of CGF was also characterized via TGA, showing consistent performance across different RS pulp loads. These findings demonstrate that the RS pulp-reinforced HEC/GG/Al CGFs are promising candidates for high-performance, eco-friendly absorbent fibrous gel foam pads in food packaging applications.

papers.title: Upconverting Y2SiO5:Yb3+-Eu3+ phosphor for luminescent and surface assisted Raman enhancement
papers.abstract: Abstract Yb3+-Eu3+ co-doped Y2SiO5 phosphor was synthesized by the co-precipitation method. The structural and optical properties of the synthesized phosphor were investigated using XRD, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, FESEM, Fluorescence microscopy, and upconversion emission studies. Photoluminescence upconverting spectra under 980 nm NIR laser diode excitation exhibited characteristic emission bands of Eu3+ ions corresponding to the 5D0→7Fj (j = 0-2) transitions. The upconverting mechanism has been explained through the energy level diagram, where, possible co-operative energy transfer takes place from Yb3+ + Yb3+ → Eu3+. The overall emission colour has been noted in the reddish-white colour region using the CIE 1931 chromaticity coordinates diagram. The synthesized phosphor is used for making a non-plasmonic SERS substrate to study the surface-assisted Raman mode enhancement by probing the RhB dye molecule. The calculated enhancement factor (EF) is ~5.52 × 102. A charge transfer-mediated mechanism has been explained by fluorescence microscopy. Experimental results indicate that Y2SiO5:Yb3+-Eu3+ phosphor is a promising material for next generation luminescent and non-plasmonic surface-assisted Raman enhancer applications.

Continuous-discrete phase and thermo-fluid-stress multi-field coupled numerical model was established for laser cladding of Fe31 powder with off-axis powder feeding on a Q235 curved substrate. The model employs a 1200 W laser power, a scanning speed of 6 mm/s, and a powder feed rate of 10 g/min. Considering the particle size distribution and the temperature-dependent thermal properties of the material, it conducts a comparative analysis of the transient evolution of powder temperature, concentration, flow velocity, as well as the temperature field, flow field, and stress field in the melt pool under both rectangular and circular beam spot conditions. The results show that, under the same total laser power, the rectangular light spot has a wider and more uniform energy distribution area, reducing the concentration of local heat input. When the laser irradiation lasts for 2 seconds, the maximum flow velocity of the rectangular light spot increases by approximately 21.1%; the maximum transient thermal stress decreases by approximately 7.9%. The rectangular light spot model was subjected to 12 repeated measurements using infrared thermal imaging experiments, and the relative error between the simulated temperature and the experimental measurement results was 1.47%. The calculations show that, rectangular light spots have a more uniform distribution of heat input, which can reduce local peak temperatures and alter the flow and stress distribution characteristics of the molten pool. This study provides a theoretical reference for the selection of different light spot shapes and the optimization of process parameters in oblique-axis powder-fed laser cladding.

papers.title: Complete monotonicity as a single-trajectory witness ofanomalous thermal relaxation
papers.abstract: Abstract Anomalous relaxation is usually identified comparatively, through crossings between distinct relaxation trajectories. Whether a single relaxation curve carries an intrinsic signature of anomalous decay has remained unclear. Here we take complete monotonicity of the relative entropy to equilibrium—its being a positive superposition of pure exponential decays—as such a signature—an intrinsic, all-orders criterion defined for any reversible relaxation, classical or quantum—and settle it exactly in the simplest nontrivial arena, the thermal qubit under a Davies generator: complete monotonicity holds if and only if (r−s)(s− 1 2 ) ≥0, where s and r are the Gibbs and initial ground populations. Heating-like relaxation is completely monotone at every order, while cooling-like relaxation carries a negative cubic Bernstein atom—a genuinely finite-temperature, modular obstruction. Initial coherence cancels it only resonantly: exactly at Γ2/Γ1 = 1 2 (T2 = 2T1), with the closed criterion |c|2 ≥(2s−1)(s−r), and in a certified window at 3 2 ; no other physical commensurate ratio restores it. The mechanism yields falsifiable predictions, including an exact dephasing onset law t∗= ln(q0/q∗ 0)/(2Γφ) for the fitted odd-class amplitude of a single relaxation curve.

X-ray diffraction analysis revealed sintering-induced structural phase transformation (order-disorder) from the unsintered monoclinic phase (space group C2/m) to the orthorhombic phase (space group Fddd) on sintering at 1200°C. This observation is corroborated by Raman spectroscopy results indicated by the absence of the characteristic soft mode in the sintered orthorhombic Li₃Co₂SbO₆ phase. Conductivity analysis, fitted using Jonscher’s power law, suggested a combination of correlated barrier hopping (CBH) and quantum mechanical tunneling (QMT) mechanisms. A Systematic structure-property correlation is evidenced and explained

papers.abstract: Abstract Magnetic hyperthermia requires nanoparticles whose heat output can be tuned while the material remains biocompatible. Here, Cr-substituted Co–Zn ferrite nanoparticles, Co 0.6 Zn 0.4 Cr x Fe 2−x O 4 (x = 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3), were synthesised by auto-combustion and calcined at 500 ο C for 2 h. X-ray diffraction confirmed a single-phase cubic spinel, with the lattice constant and crystallite size decreasing from 8.4039 Å and 34 nm to 8.3947 Å and 25 nm as the smaller Cr 3+ ions replaced Fe 3+ , and electron-microscopy particle diameters decreased from 38.55 to 31.96 nm. Cr substitution reduced the saturation magnetisation from 58.73 to 36.13 A m 2 kg −1 and the effective anisotropy constant from 134.5 to 82.4 kJ m −3 , lowering the anisotropy energy barrier to 0.35 of its unsubstituted value, with the decreases in particle volume and anisotropy contributing about equally. Under a field of 14.92 kA m −1 at 337 kHz, the specific absorption rate (SAR) at 0.5 mg mL −1 decreased from 342 to 251 W g −1 and the intrinsic loss power from 4.57 to 3.34 nH m 2 kg −1 . SAR was higher at 0.5 than at 1 mg mL −1 for every composition, consistent with interparticle interactions. After a 600 s exposure, the unsubstituted sample exceeded 47 ο C at both concentrations, whereas the x = 0.3 sample at 0.5 mg mL −1 reached 46.47 ο C, within the 42–47 ο C therapeutic range, with the temperature still rising at the end of the exposure. In vitro assays showed less than 4% haemolysis for all samples and cell viabilities above 90% for the higher-Cr samples. papers.title: Inter-cavity flame dynamics for ignition and flameholding in a dual-cavity scramjet
papers.abstract: To investigate the effects of ignition position on flame propagation and combustion characteristics in a dual-cavity scramjet combustor, comparative experiments were conducted under upstream cavity ignition (UCI) and downstream cavity ignition (DCI) conditions in a direct-connect supersonic combustor facility at an inflow Mach number of 2.52. Synchronized schlieren and CH* chemiluminescence imaging systems were employed to visualize flow and flame dynamics during ignition and flameholding processes. For both ignition positions in the present study, the flame initially propagates downstream, then migrates upstream, and finally stabilizes above the upstream cavity. During inter-cavity propagation, the flame leading edge anchors in the near-wall low-velocity zone, and the flame propagation path within the unignited cavity follows the local recirculation direction. Combustion-induced backpressure shifts the shock train upstream; the resulting shock–flame interaction enhances flame propagation toward the unignited cavity and intensifies combustion during the first inter-cavity propagation in the DCI case, whereas this phenomenon is not observed in the UCI case. During flameholding, both cases exhibit cyclic oscillations with temporary flame weakening near the downstream cavity. Under UCI, the oscillation frequency progressively increases until premature flameout occurs, while under DCI, the frequency remains lower without acceleration; both cavities provide stronger flame stabilization, and the flame leading edge oscillates over a smaller range.

papers.title: Wavenumber-frequency spectrum diagnostic method for aerodynamic instability precursors in confined compressible jets: From spectral precursors to vortex-wave mechanisms
papers.abstract: A confined compressible jet can undergo aerodynamic instability through coupled shear-layer amplification, wave forcing, and pressure-wave redistribution. Conventional single-point pressure spectra cannot distinguish spatial organization from propagation, limiting mechanistic diagnosis. This study combines pressure-array wavenumber-frequency (k − f) spectra with large-eddy-simulation diagnostics to examine operating-condition-dependent spectral reorganization in a generic compressible-gas Laval-tube special valve. Each condition uses a 20-cycle pressure record. The typical and 363.15 K low-frequency conditions each include three independent seed-perturbed realizations. Their realization-mean dominant frequencies are fp = 111.08 ± 0.30 and 94.04 ± 0.44 Hz, respectively; all three values at 363.15 K remain below those of the typical condition, confirming that the frequency depression exceeds the tested seed variability. Increasing pressure drop raises fp to 1165.23 Hz and changes the signed spectral occupancy, accompanied by expanded acceleration, localized Ma > 1, and vorticity footprints. Opening variation reorganizes the downstream response path and produces a nonmonotonic frequency sequence over 40%–100% opening. Across the pressure-drop, opening, and temperature sweeps, the spectral response is interpreted jointly with jet acceleration, compressibility, vorticity, and resolved turbulent-energy redistribution. Conditional phase-velocity estimates are 22.83 ± 0.50 m/s for the typical condition and 33.64 ± 0.44 m/s at 363.15 K. However, only one typical-condition realization and none at 363.15 K passes the complete phase/coherence gate, so an ensemble propagation direction is not assigned. The k–f spectrum therefore provides a physical diagnostic of flow reorganization rather than stand-alone evidence of propagation. Time-resolved pressure-array measurements remain necessary to validate the unsteady diagnostics.

papers.title: Line-tension effect on the equilibrium and stability of a spherical floating particle at a fluid–fluid interface
papers.abstract: A recent matched-asymptotic framework for a spherical particle floating at a fluid–fluid interface reduced the coupled Young equation and vertical force balance to a single nonlinear equation but assumed a constant macroscopic Young angle. We extend the framework to include line tension. A variational derivation places the dimensionless line tension κ=k/(r0σ), the ratio of the line tension k to the product of the sphere radius r0 and the surface tension σ, in the modified Young equation. Because the line-tension energy depends on the filling angle alone and that angle is set by the modified Young equation, the line-tension term drops out of the vertical force balance identically. The coupled system reduces to a single substitution of the constant contact angle by a filling-angle dependent contact angle. Closed-form first-order corrections agree with the numerical solution of the nonlinear asymptotic equilibrium equation with O(κ2) remainders away from the floatability boundary, and the line-tension response of the framework is confirmed independently by a direct numerical solution of the Young–Laplace equation that shares no asymptotic ingredient. The hydrophilic regime is about an order of magnitude more sensitive to κ than the hydrophobic one across the full range of contact angles. The modified Young equation rewrites as a linear regression that recovers k from multi-sphere datasets, and its regression form is shown to be consistent with the original droplet dataset of Klauser and coworkers.

summary_zh.motivation: 探究升力板对亚声速冲击射流声学反馈回路的影响。
summary_zh.method: 采用高保真大涡模拟对比有/无升力板两种冲击射流工况。
summary_zh.result: 升力板改变反馈模态阶数并使峰值声压级提高7 dB。
summary_zh.validation: 通过LES结果与Powell反馈回路模型预测相互印证。

summary_en.motivation: The study aims to clarify how a lift plate alters the aeroacoustic feedback loop of subsonic impinging jets.
summary_en.method: Two impinging jet configurations with and without a lift plate are simulated using high-fidelity large-eddy simulation.
summary_en.result: The lift plate shifts the dominant Strouhal number and feedback modal order while raising the peak sound pressure level by 7 dB.
summary_en.validation: The LES predictions are cross-checked against lip-line RMS velocity peaks, standing-wave node counts, and the Powell feedback-loop model.
